title: Manna
lead: The bread God gave Israel in the wilderness for forty years (Exodus 16; Numbers 11). Psalms call it the grain of heaven, Jesus calls himself the true bread from heaven (John 6), and Revelation promises hidden manna.

sections.b: Manna appears first in Exodus 16 and is described again in Numbers 11:7–9, where the people tire of it and long for Egypt's meat. It stops the day after Israel eats the produce of Canaan (Joshua 5:12). The Psalms call it "grain of heaven" and "bread of the mighty" (Psalm 78:24–25; Psalm 105:40), and Nehemiah 9:20 thanks God for it in a prayer of confession. Jesus feeds crowds in the wilderness and then calls himself "the bread of life" that comes down from heaven, better than the manna the ancestors ate and died (John 6:31–58). Paul calls it "spiritual food" (1 Corinthians 10:3), Hebrews 9:4 places a jar of it in the ark, and Revelation 2:17 promises "hidden manna" to the one who overcomes.
